title: Upper Zone Sensor Error
shortDescription: The upper-zone temperature sensor is reading out of range.
fullDescription:
Samsung dual-zone wine coolers use separate NTC thermistors for the upper and lower compartments. Code 1E indicates the upper sensor is open, shorted, or disconnected.

Without a valid reading the upper zone falls back to a default temperature curve and can drift out of spec.

fixSteps.title: Access sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug, empty upper rack, remove interior plastic cover to expose sensor.

fixSteps.title: Test and swap
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance (around 5 kOhm at room temp). Replace if open or shorted.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if replacement does not clear the code, since the main PCB could be at fault.

faq.a: Briefly yes, but correct temperature is critical for long aging.

title: Lower Zone Sensor Error
shortDescription: The lower-zone temperature sensor is faulty.
fullDescription:
2E is the mirror of 1E but for the lower compartment thermistor. The lower zone is where red wines are typically stored at 14-18C.

Incorrect readings can either overcool or undercool the lower zone, both of which harm long-term storage.

fixSteps.title: Empty lower zone
fixSteps.instruction: Remove bottles and shelves to access the rear interior wall.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Unclip old sensor, connect new one in the same position, route wiring via existing channel.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the thermistor wiring is routed through foam behind the rear wall.

faq.a: For a few days yes. Longer risks spoiling wine at the wrong temp.

title: Ambient Sensor Error
shortDescription: The cabinet ambient sensor has failed.
fullDescription:
Code 3E indicates the ambient thermistor (measuring kitchen temperature) is out of range. Samsung uses this reading to adjust compressor cycles when the kitchen is hot or cold.

The cooler will continue to operate but may be less efficient.

fixSteps.title: Remove rear access panel
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and pull the cooler out, then remove the upper rear panel.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the old sensor from its clip and install the new one.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the unit is built in and cannot be pulled out without cabinet work.

faq.a: Not immediately. The compartments still run on their own sensors.

title: Humidity Sensor Error
shortDescription: The interior humidity sensor is reporting bad data.
fullDescription:
Premium Samsung wine cabinets monitor compartment humidity to protect corks. 4E means the humidity sensor has failed or is disconnected.

Operation continues but humidity management (water tray activation, etc.) is disabled.

fixSteps.title: Let cabinet dry
fixSteps.instruction: If condensation suspected, unplug 24 hours with door ajar.

fixSteps.title: Replace module
fixSteps.instruction: If error persists, install a new humidity sensor module.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the sensor is integrated into the PCB and requires board replacement.

faq.a: Yes, dry air can dry corks and let oxygen in over years.

title: Defrost Sensor Error
shortDescription: The defrost thermistor is open circuit.
fullDescription:
6E signals an open defrost sensor. Samsung wine coolers with forced-air evaporators run brief defrost cycles that rely on this sensor to terminate.

A broken wire at the connector strain relief is the most common cause.

fixSteps.title: Access evaporator
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug cooler, empty top compartment, remove rear interior panel.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Unclip old sensor from evaporator tube and install a new one in same position.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if wiring is routed through foam and requires special tools to reroute.

faq.a: Not directly, but blocked airflow will destabilize temperature.

title: LED / Light Circuit Error
shortDescription: The interior LED lighting circuit has faulted.
fullDescription:
7E is triggered when the LED driver reports an open or short. Interior lighting will be off but cooling continues normally.

It is safe to run the cooler with 7E until a part can be ordered.

fixSteps.title: Replace LED strip
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug, remove side trim, disconnect old LED strip and install new one with matching connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace driver
fixSteps.instruction: If new strip does not light, swap the driver module behind the control board.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if trim is glued in place and risks breaking during removal.

title: Evaporator Fan Error
shortDescription: The internal circulation fan has stalled.
fullDescription:
22E means the evaporator fan motor tachometer is silent. The fan moves chilled air across both zones.

With no circulation, compartments stratify and cooling becomes uneven. Ice buildup on the fan blade is the most frequent cause.

fixSteps.title: Defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug cooler and leave door open 6 hours to melt any ice.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: If 22E returns after defrost, install a new evaporator fan motor.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if you are uncomfortable working around the evaporator tubing.

faq.a: Only if the motor itself is fine. If bearings failed it must be replaced.

title: Defrost Heater Error
shortDescription: The defrost heater did not raise temperature during its cycle.
fullDescription:
33E is logged when a defrost cycle finishes with no noticeable temperature rise at the evaporator. The heater is likely open, or the thermal fuse has tripped.

Uncorrected, frost will slowly choke the evaporator.

fixSteps.title: Full defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and leave door open 8-12 hours.

fixSteps.title: Replace heater and fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect heater leads, install new heater and thermal fuse together.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the heater is molded into the evaporator and not field serviceable.

faq.a: No, that removes an important safety feature.

title: Inverter Compressor Error
shortDescription: The inverter compressor driver reports a fault.
fullDescription:
88E (similar to 83E on freezers) means the inverter PCB reports lock-rotor, over-current, or communication fault with the compressor. The cabinet will warm up because cooling stops.

Inspection by a sealed-system technician is usually required.

fixSteps.title: Check voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Verify outlet is supplying correct mains voltage.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 15 minutes and restore.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: If 88E returns, book a technician to test the inverter and compressor.

whenToCallPro: Always if 88E persists. Compressor work involves refrigerant.

faq.a: Yes, to any cool dark place while you wait for service.

title: Power Interruption Alert
shortDescription: A recent power outage was detected.
fullDescription:
PE is informational and appears after any power loss so you can evaluate wine storage. Press any button to dismiss.

Frequent PE events can indicate a loose plug, a weak outlet, or a flaky GFCI.

fixSteps.title: Dismiss alert
fixSteps.instruction: Press any button to clear PE.

fixSteps.title: Secure plug
fixSteps.instruction: Firmly reseat the power cord and avoid sharing the circuit with heavy loads.

whenToCallPro: Call an electrician only if PE is frequent despite a known-good outlet.

faq.q: Is wine ruined after an outage?
faq.a: Short outages rarely harm wine. Multi-hour outages with cabinet above 20C can be a concern for long-aged bottles.
